# HubVibe -- machine-payable services for autonomous agents

> A machine-service gateway: site compliance audits plus a catalog of
> per-call capabilities -- LLM inference, web search and extraction,
> blockchain/market/prediction-market data, media generation, sandboxed
> compute, composite research -- every one paid per call over HTTP 402
> with no account and no human in the loop. The audits are deterministic
> checks against the actual page; a check that couldn't run is never
> reported as a false pass, and a call that produced no result is never
> billed.

Base URL: https://hubvibe-io.com

Machine-readable discovery:
- /.well-known/agent.json -- full manifest: pricing, live payment rails,
  rate limits, per-endpoint examples
- /openapi.json -- OpenAPI 3.1 spec for all routes, with a response schema
  and example on every /work route
- /.well-known/ard.json -- Agentic Resource Discovery manifest: one entry
  per audit and per worker with capabilities and representative queries
- /mcp -- live MCP endpoint (Streamable HTTP, JSON-RPC). Discovery via
  initialize/tools/list is free; tools/call is billed per call. It speaks
  the x402 MCP protocol: an unpaid tools/call returns isError with the v2
  PaymentRequired in structuredContent; send the signed PaymentPayload in
  params._meta["x402/payment"] (the x402.mcp client does this for you) and
  the settlement receipt comes back in the result's
  _meta["x402/payment-response"]. X-PAYMENT / PAYMENT-SIGNATURE / X-API-Key
  headers on the POST work as well.
- /mcp.json -- static MCP tool definitions with their httpEndpoint
- /docs -- interactive API reference

Rate limit: 600 requests/minute per API key (or per IP for x402/MPP
callers). Exceeding it returns HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header and
nothing is billed -- the limit is checked before any payment is settled.

## Endpoints

All endpoints below are POST, priced per call, and accept a Stripe API
key, an x402 on-chain payment, or an MPP (Machine Payments Protocol)
payment. There is no free tier and no unauthenticated access: every audit
costs a real browser page load, so every audit is paid for.

- POST /audit/wcag -- $0.05 -- Website accessibility audit (a11y, WCAG compliance check): WCAG 2.1 level
  A and AA conformance of any live URL or raw HTML, tested with axe-core
  in a real headless browser. Returns every violation with rule id,
  impact, help text and affected node count. Deterministic rules; a check
  that cannot run returns an error, never a pass.
  Input: {"html": "string (optional)", "url": "string (optional, one of html/url required)"}

- POST /audit/seo -- $0.05 -- SEO audit of a web page (on-page SEO check) for any live URL or raw HTML:
  title tag, meta description, H1 heading structure, canonical link,
  OpenGraph and social tags, JSON-LD structured data, html lang attribute.
  Rule-by-rule findings with severity and what is missing or malformed.
  Input: {"html": "string (optional)", "url": "string (optional, one of html/url required)"}

- POST /audit/security -- $0.05 -- Security headers check for a website: audits HTTPS, HSTS, Content-
  Security-Policy (CSP), X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options /
  clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy and CORS from the real HTTP
  response of any live URL. Findings with severity for what is missing.
  Header posture only, not a penetration test.
  Input: {"url": "string (required)"}

- POST /audit/performance -- $0.05 -- Page speed and page weight audit of a web page from one real browser load:
  total bytes transferred, HTTP request count and DOM node count, measured
  rather than estimated, with findings when the page is heavy. Page-weight
  signals, not Core Web Vitals.
  Input: {"url": "string (required)"}

- POST /audit/bundle -- $0.15 -- Full website audit in one call: accessibility (WCAG 2.1 A/AA via axe-
  core), on-page SEO, HTTP security headers and page speed / page weight,
  from a single browser load of one URL. Cheaper than four separate calls;
  if any part cannot run, nothing is billed.
  Input: {"url": "string (required)"}

- POST /audit -- $0.05 -- Alias of /audit/wcag, kept for backward compatibility.

## Worker network (/work/*) -- completed work

Priced per call on the same HTTP 402 rail as the audits. GET /work (free)
lists every worker live on this node with its price, tier, input schema and
what it returns; a worker whose provider is not configured is listed as
unavailable and never quoted. Send an Idempotency-Key header to make a retry
safe: a repeated key returns the stored result and is not charged again.

Utility (one live read, $0.02-$0.10):
- POST /work/chain/network -- Base mainnet block height and gas price
- POST /work/chain/address -- one Base address: balance, transaction count,
  contract or wallet
- POST /work/chain/transaction -- one Base transaction with its receipt
- POST /work/chain/rpc -- generic allowlisted read-only JSON-RPC on Base
- POST /work/market/quote -- live Coinbase spot price and 24h change
- POST /work/market/rates -- Coinbase exchange-rate table for one currency
- POST /work/market/ticker -- live bid/ask/volume from Coinbase's Exchange
  data host (independent of market/quote)
- POST /work/market/prediction -- live Polymarket markets as implied
  probabilities
- POST /work/prediction/market -- one Polymarket market by slug
- POST /work/prediction/events -- live Polymarket events by volume
- POST /work/extract/page -- readable text, title and links from any page,
  rendered in a real browser
- POST /work/fetch/raw -- raw HTTP fetch: status, headers, body, any status
  code (unlike extract/page, a 404/500 from the target is a result)
- POST /work/search/web -- live web search, grounded via Gemini's Google
  Search tool
- POST /work/maps/places -- search places via Google's managed Maps
  Grounding Lite MCP server (needs an operator-set key)
- POST /work/maps/route -- directions between two places (same server)
- POST /work/maps/weather -- weather at a named place (same server)

Standard (inference and data, $0.25-$0.50):
- POST /work/llm/analyze -- answer a question from text you supply, saying
  so when the text does not contain the answer (Gemini)
- POST /work/llm/extract -- named fields from text as JSON, null when not
  stated (Gemini)
- POST /work/llm/generate -- raw completion, your prompt and model choice
  (Gemini; Claude via Vertex Model Garden once enabled)
- POST /work/code/execute -- run Python in Google's own hosted sandbox
- POST /work/image/generate -- one image from a text prompt (Imagen 4)
- POST /work/speech/synthesize -- text to speech (Cloud Text-to-Speech)
- POST /work/speech/transcribe -- speech to text, up to 60s/10MB (STT v2)
- POST /work/data/query -- read-only BigQuery SQL, including Google's public
  datasets, under a scan ceiling
- POST /work/monitor/snapshot -- save a page as a baseline to check later
- POST /work/monitor/check -- re-fetch a baselined page and get a change
  summary

Advanced (several providers, one completed result, $5.00):
- POST /work/data/question -- a plain-language question about a BigQuery
  table, answered with the SQL and the rows behind it
- POST /work/research/brief -- read a web page and answer a question about it
- POST /work/research/page_facts -- the fields you name from a web page, as
  JSON
- POST /work/research/web -- a live web search, read, and a cited answer
- POST /work/verify/claims -- specific claims checked against specific
  sources: supported / contradicted / unsupported, with the quote
- POST /work/market/intel -- a live spot quote and prediction-market
  probabilities on one subject, analysed together (market data, not advice)
- POST /work/security/mcp_inspect -- probe a customer's MCP endpoint's
  handshake: auth posture, protocol version, tools not marked read-only

Premium ($10.00):
- POST /work/data/forecast -- forecast a BigQuery time series (AI.FORECAST,
  TimesFM, no training)
- POST /work/data/anomalies -- detect anomalies in a BigQuery time series
  (AI.DETECT_ANOMALIES)
- POST /work/research/company -- a cited research brief on a company from
  live web sources
- POST /work/video/generate -- a short video from a text prompt (Veo, once
  the operator has verified the model on this deployment)

Same payment gate and the same guarantees as the audits: an
unauthenticated call answers HTTP 402 with the price, requests are
validated before any payment is read, and a call no provider could
complete returns HTTP 502 with per-provider reasons and bills nothing.
Input schemas and prices for every live worker are in
/.well-known/agent.json and the /mcp tools/list.

## Payment and auth

Up to three rails, all fail-closed (no valid credential/payment means no
audit runs, and nothing partially executes on a rejected payment):

1. API key -- `X-API-Key` header: a prepaid key bought through the MPP
   top-up rail (a $0.50 block, spent at the per-call rates). There are no
   subscriptions; machine callers should use the per-call rails below.
2. x402 -- on-chain payment via the x402 protocol; verified and settled
   through a facilitator, never trusted client-side.
3. MPP (Machine Payments Protocol) -- Stripe Shared Payment Tokens (fiat)
   or Tempo network (crypto), co-authored by Stripe and Tempo.

Which of these are actually live is deployment-specific. Do not assume:
read the `accepts` array in any 402 response body, or `payment.methods` in
/.well-known/agent.json. Both list only rails that can genuinely settle
right now -- a rail that isn't configured is omitted rather than advertised
with a null recipient.

An unauthenticated POST to any paid route returns HTTP 402 carrying that
`accepts` array plus, for MPP, one signed `WWW-Authenticate: Payment`
challenge per method. That is the intended discovery path for an agent:
call the endpoint, read the price and rails off the 402, pay, retry.

## What you are charged for

Only an audit that produced a result. An x402 payment is verified in order
to grant access, but is not settled until the audit has actually delivered
-- so an audit that fails to run (unreachable target, timeout) returns HTTP
502 and costs nothing. A rate-limited request returns 429 and also costs
nothing, because the limit is checked before any payment is touched.

## Integrations

Source for these lives in the repo, not on this server -- they are
client-side wrappers around the endpoints above, not additional routes:
https://github.com/its-fortunatefolly/hubvibe/tree/main/wcag-audit-engine/integrations

- langchain_tool.py -- LangChain tool wrapper
- github_action.yml -- GitHub Action for CI audit-on-push
- mcp_server.py -- MCP server using the official Model Context Protocol
  SDK; standalone script with its own requirements.txt, not part of this
  deployed service (its dependencies conflict with this service's FastAPI
  version) -- see that file's docstring for setup.

## Pricing

Machine, per call (this is the product): $0.05 per single-dimension audit,
$0.15 per bundle. No account, no minimum.

There are no subscriptions: per call is the only price.
See /.well-known/agent.json for the authoritative live pricing.
